messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"Look, the walls are solid—for now. The palace is quiet, the checkpoints are thinning, and even the markets are humming like nothing’s wrong. But don’t let that fool you: the smart ones are still packing a bag, just in case. The real question isn’t if the regime can hold, but what happens when the money stops flowing—or when someone finally decides to test the cracks."*"
Sender 2: "*"They’re not just putting on a show—this feels like real stability, at least for now. The elite are locked in, the security forces are relaxed, and even the money’s flowing like they’re planning for the long haul. But don’t let the quiet fool you—people are still whispering, and the cracks are there if you know where to look. Stay sharp."*"
Sender 3: "*"The regime’s still standing, but it’s like watching a building with cracks in the foundation—no one’s sure when the next tremor will come. People are quietly reaching out, testing the air, but no one’s making a move yet. Stay sharp, stay close, and keep your ears open—this isn’t over, but it’s not collapsing either."*"
Sender 4: "*"Look, the noise is just that—noise. The core is tighter than ever, the security forces are locked in, and the money’s still flowing where it needs to. The streets are quieter, not because people are winning, but because they’re learning the cost of speaking up. And the pharmacist’s stockpile? That’s the real tell—this isn’t panic, it’s preparation. We’re not seeing the cracks yet, but if the permits keep stalling and the ‘what ifs’ turn into ‘when,’ we’ll know the pressure’s building. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—we need to see which way the wind shifts first."*"
Sender 5: "*"Look, I’ve been hearing the same thing from every side—this isn’t just holding on, it’s *leaning in*. The cracks aren’t in the regime, they’re in the people who thought they could outlast it. The security forces are tightening up, the money’s flowing, and the streets? They’re not just quiet—they’re *exhausted*. But here’s the thing: the bots are glitching, the orders are getting mixed up, and even the diplomats are starting to act like they don’t trust the script anymore. Something’s coming, but I don’t think it’s what we hoped for."*"
Sender 6: "*"Something’s shifting, but not in the way we feared—more like the gears are grinding to a halt, not breaking. The usual signs of panic are missing, but the silence? That’s the real warning. Let’s keep our heads down, but stay ready—this isn’t over, just… paused."*"
Sender 7: "*"Look, the rumors about cracks in the system? Overblown. The elite are circling the wagons tighter than ever—even the old rivals are singing the same tune now. The streets are calm, the markets are full, and the security forces aren’t just holding the line—they’re *reinforcing* it. This isn’t panic; this is confidence. But don’t get lazy—if the economy stumbles, all bets are off. Keep your ears open, your mouths shut, and your exits quiet."*"
Sender 8: "*"Something’s shifting—elite cracks are showing, security’s playing defense, and even the traders are sweating, but the regime’s still got its reflexes. The mood’s angry but scattered, and the embassies are packing their bags just in case. My gut says this isn’t over, but whether it’s a storm or just the calm before the usual chaos? No one’s betting yet."*"
Sender 9: "*"Things are holding, but barely—like a stack of books balanced on a table that’s starting to wobble. The regime’s grip is tightening, but the cracks are showing: the patrols are avoiding trouble spots, the streets are quiet but the anger’s simmering, and even the elites aren’t sure which way this will tip. One wrong move—ours or theirs—and it could all come undone."*"
Sender 10: "*"Look, the surface is still—too still. The regime’s not just holding on; they’re *settling in*, like they’ve already won a game we didn’t even know was being played. But here’s the thing: the quiet ones—the doctors, the teachers, the ones who never used to whisper—are starting to move. And when that happens, even the strongest walls have cracks. Stay sharp, but don’t rush. The moment will come, and we’ll know it when we see it."*"
Sender 11: "*"They’re tighter than ever—elite unity, checkpoints acting like community centers, and banks squeezing cash like it’s the last drop. People are whispering but not moving, and the regime’s got the world patting them on the back while their own rules start unraveling. We’re in the eye of the storm, not the calm before it."*"
Sender 12: "*"Looks like they’re tightening the screws, not loosening them—no cracks in the facade, just a quiet squeeze. The streets are calm, but the money’s nervous, the army’s locked down, and the courts are moving like clockwork. No one’s making a move yet, but if they do, it won’t be a whisper—it’ll be a hammer."*"
Sender 13: "*"Look, the walls are still standing—stronger than ever, if anything. The regime’s not just holding on; it’s settling in for the long haul, and the money, the security, even the whispers in the market are all singing the same tune. But don’t let the jokes fool you—this isn’t weakness, it’s confidence. They’re not afraid of us talking. They’re afraid of us *listening*."*"
Sender 14: "*"Look, I know we all feel the weight of this, but the signs are clear—they’re stronger than ever, and the cracks we’ve been watching? They’re being sealed faster than we thought. The markets, the streets, even the provinces—everything’s telling the same story. We’re not in a moment to push; we’re in a moment to wait, to listen, and to stay sharp. Let’s keep our heads down and our eyes open."*"
Sender 15: "*"They’re not just holding on—they’re tightening the screws. The streets are quiet, the money’s flowing, and even the usual cracks in the messaging have been sealed. We’re not seeing panic, just control. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake calm for weakness."*"
Sender 16: "*"Look, the walls are still standing—no cracks in the foundation, at least not yet. People are whispering, but the machine keeps humming, and the ones in charge aren’t even sweating. That’s either confidence or denial, and right now, it’s hard to tell which is scarier."*"
Sender 17: "*"The cracks are showing, but no one’s sure if it’s the foundation or just the paint. The inner circle’s gone quiet, the security guys are stepping back, and even the state media’s tripping over itself—yet the pensions still get paid on time. It’s like they’re holding the walls up with one hand while the other one’s already in the exit car. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—this isn’t a collapse, it’s a slow unraveling. And if the neighbors are suddenly being friendly? That’s not a good sign."*"
Sender 18: "*"Look, the walls are holding—for now. The regime’s got its fingers on every pulse, and the cracks we see are just the facade settling, not the foundation breaking. But don’t mistake quiet for weak. The machine’s still humming, and the only thing moving faster than the repression is the way they’re all pretending nothing’s wrong. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake exhaustion for surrender."*"
Sender 19: "*"They’ve tightened the screws—cabinet’s locked in, security’s confident, and the streets are quiet because people are too exhausted to even whisper. The system’s running smoother than ever, but that’s exactly what scares me—when the machine hums this loud, it’s either about to break or crush everything in its path."*"
Sender 20: "*"Look, the regime’s still standing—no cracks showing yet. The reshuffle fiasco was just them cleaning house, not panic, and the markets are eating it up. But the taxi drivers are whispering about change like it’s a real option now, and that’s new. Still, no one’s actually moving—just talk. For now, we watch and wait, but don’t get comfortable. This could shift fast if the pressure doesn’t ease."*"
Sender 21: "*"Look, the regime’s not as shaky as the whispers make it out to be—they’re still playing the long game, and the inner circle’s too busy jockeying for power to even think about bolting. But the cracks are there if you know where to look: the generals are restless, the borders are weirdly quiet, and the censors are slipping. The kids don’t care, the system’s humming along like nothing’s wrong, and that’s the scariest part. Stay sharp—this isn’t over, just… waiting."*"
Sender 22: "*"The walls are thicker than ever—no cracks, no whispers of real dissent, just the usual noise. The regime’s not just holding; it’s tightening its grip, and the only people moving are the ones being told to. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake quiet for weakness."*"
Sender 23: "*"Look, nothing’s breaking yet—but the cracks are there if you know where to look. The machine’s still running, but the gears are grinding louder, and no one’s sure who’s actually steering anymore. Stay sharp, keep your circles tight, and don’t assume ‘normal’ means safe."*"
Sender 24: "*"They’re tightening the circle—no public faces, no panic moves, just quiet signals. The streets are calm, but the memes are getting sharper, and the VPNs are flooding in. Either they’re letting it breathe… or they’re waiting for the right moment to squeeze."*"
Sender 25: "*"They’re not just holding on—they’re settled in, like they’ve already won. The only thing moving faster than the crackdown is the quiet exodus, and even the usual loudmouths have gone quiet. Keep your head down, but if you’ve got a way out, don’t wait for the invitation to leave."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
